I have been farming these 9.5 mu in Quzhou for 35 years, and I know what this land can do. Cotton is my main crop and my steady income—the cotton buyer has come to our village every autumn for as long as I can remember. I will plant 5 mu of improved cotton in April with rotary tillage. I apply compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with nitrogen at flowering and boll-setting. With my well, I irrigate twice: once at flowering and once at boll filling. Cotton pests are relentless here—bollworm, aphids, mites—so I spray about 16 times through the season. I expect around 550 jin per mu.

Stevia brings good cash and the processing company collects it from the village. I will set aside 2.5 mu for improved stevia, planted in April. It needs more water and more potassium than cotton, so I irrigate 5 times and put down extra potash to keep the leaves thick. I spray about 9 times for leaf pests. It should yield about 550 jin per mu and be ready by August, which lets me focus on cotton harvest after that.

For cauliflower, I will plant 2 mu in autumn—July or August transplanting after the early crops come off. Autumn cauliflower fetches better prices at market. I use improved seedlings, rotary tillage, and plenty of fertilizer—cauliflower is hungry, especially for nitrogen. I irrigate 4 times and spray 5 times for cabbage worms and downy mildew. I expect about 6,000 jin per mu by late autumn.

This way my labor is spread: stevia finishes in August, cotton occupies the summer and autumn, and cauliflower fills the autumn gap.
